author: GamingBolt
description:
The developer also preserves the original’s gritty Lord of the Ring’s atmosphere despite sharpening the fidelity in The Lord of the Rings War in the North Legacy. The port’s issues, really, are foundational. In other words: they’re unchangeable unless a more thorough revamp was undertaken. 

Long, repetitive level design and enemy encounters, awkward cameras, functional combat – these can’t be as readily improved as HUD and technical performance can. Whether there’s an audience sizeable enough for a Lord of the Rings game whose legacy is overshadowed by a pair Middle-Earth titles is debateable, but there’s an irony here as Lord of the Rings: War in the North is exactly the kind of game that should be remade as what was originally there proved enough to capture a cult following.
title: The Lord of the Rings War in the North Legacy Edition Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Mortal Shell 2 is all set to take the Soulslike scene by storm when it debuts in a few days, and we say that with good reasons. We’ve been quite impressed with our time in its grim and gritty world, while the Shells have managed to make its combat a brutal, fast-paced affair.

Of course, games like these often like to stay aloof, letting you figure things out for yourself, and that’s very much the case here. But we’re here to help you out just enough to make your adventure make a little more sense when you’re getting started. Join us as we take you through a few things to keep in mind when you’re starting out as the Harbinger.
title: Mortal Shell 2 - 15 Things I Wish I Knew Before Playing It

author: GamingBolt
description:
PlayStation, in all its disc-hating glory (don't look at me – check the chat replay for yourself), debuted a new State of Play recently, but the star was a single game: Phantom Blade Zero. Following a very impressive extended trailer, which developer S-Game assured was just the beginning, the Deep Dive showcased a lot more new gameplay.

There was a lot to take in, from the world's scale and the sheer variety of weapons to the utter poetry in motion that is combat – including boss fights like the Lion Dance Grandmaster, which you have to see. We received a closer look at the locations that make up the Phantom World – serene environments contrasting with dark warehouses with dozens of hanging puppets and ominous towers where foul experiments take place. And let's not forget S-Game's rather clever take on permadeath mode.
title: Phantom Blade Zero Is Now Becoming Impossible to IGNORE
